html:
SMTO-FIL-0036 — Part of the file arrived in an unexpected form during the copy

GUID: f2dcb4b7-c0d2-4d44-8a8d-ba16d4c5a8bf
Slug: file-invalid-transfer-chunk
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • While copying a file between Gateways, one piece of the file didn't have the expected size or position, or didn't match the original file. SMTO stopped the copy before putting the file in place at the destination.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure no program is still writing to the original file, and wait until it is finished. If the file changes while it is being read, its pieces no longer match the original.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and use Check for updates on both Gateways. Gateways on different versions can split the file into pieces in ways that don't match.
  3. Ask SMTO in the conversation to show the size and last-modified time of the file at the destination and of the original file, and compare them. If the destination file is already there and matches, the copy doesn't need to be repeated.
  4. If the destination file is missing or still the old version, ask SMTO to copy it again. A fresh copy reads the file from the start in matching pieces.

What success looks like

  • The new copy finishes and SMTO reports the file was copied and verified.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateways. Don't keep repeating the copy if it fails the same way; the Gateways need to be checked first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway copy rejected a chunk: a negotiated max_chunk_size was not a positive integer, a source_read reply had inconsistent encoding, length, offset, revision or size, or the destination received an empty chunk or one larger than CHUNK_SIZE (1 MiB).

What this means

  • A chunk capability limit is invalid, source chunk encoding/length/offset/revision/size is inconsistent, or the destination chunk is empty or exceeds CHUNK_SIZE. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A chunk capability limit is invalid, source chunk encoding/length/offset/revision/size is inconsistent, or the destination chunk is empty or exceeds CHUNK_SIZE.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect bounded chunk metadata and advertised limits without dumping file content.

How to fix it

  • Compare controller and Gateway versions (CHUNK_SIZE, LEGACY_CHUNK_SIZE and binary_transfer support in transfer_contract) and check whether the source file changed during the read. The relay aborts before destination_commit; confirm stage cleanup with destination_status, then start a new copy rather than resending chunks.
  • Settle the rejected transfer state and correct its chunk/protocol mismatch before supported continuation or new transfer work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The owned transfer uses validated chunks with exact sequential offsets and unchanged source identity.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
